newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open steady to firmer.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open steady to firmer Monday in line with a barely changed LME copper market.
COMEX July copper was called unchanged to up 0.20 cent from Friday's finish of 120.60 cents a lb after trading from 120.20 to 120.80 on ACCESS.
LME warehouse copper stocks fell 1,875 tonnes to 123,775 tonnes in Monday's data, while COMEX copper stocks were up 678 short tons at 46,642 short tons Friday.

COMEX stocks have been rising recently as LME stocks have fallen, but not all the COMEX stock rise could be attributed to arbitrage-related shipments from LME warehouses, and could also be indicative of the surge in copper imports into the U.S. while exports have fallen, analysts said.
Meanwhile, the strike at Inco in Canada, which began June 2, continued this week and will deprive the market of 9,000 tonnes a month of copper if it lasts.
